reception: A small citation record splits between two communities. In graphics architecture, a power-aware reconfigurable rendering engine adopted the idea of reallocating pipeline resources, work on dynamic reconfigurable shaders for embedded graphics positions itself against the compile-time approach, and GRAMPS and later work on fine-grain scheduling of pipeline parallelism cite the paper as an example of mapping the graphics pipeline onto programmable parallel hardware. In the streaming community, its rendering workloads reappear as benchmarks for mapping stream programs to multicore processors. Most mentions are brief, and the paper reads in the literature as a data point on reconfigurable rendering rather than a foundation later systems built on.
